newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bertrand Faure sees better 1996 H2.
newsitem.headline: Bertrand Faure sees better 1996 H2.

text.p: French equipment supplier Bertrand Faure said on Friday it expected to show a higher profit for 1996 and a sharply improved second half.
It confirmed it still wants to sell its Delsey luggage and Ratier-Figeac aerospace units.

Chairman Daniel Dewavrin also said Bertrand Faure's biggest shareholder Michel Thierry was still seeking to sell his 17.5 percent stake, but he said the company had not been in contact with Canadian car parts supplier Magna International.
A report that Magna was eyeing Bertrand Faure, a specialist in car seats, lifted the share price in May.

Although Bertraud Faure's production is traditionally slower in the second half than in the first, Philippe Douay, deputy managing director in charge of finances, told reporters the deterioration seen last year would not be repeated.
The company reported a 130.3 million franc 1995 first-half profit but earned just 92.3 million francs for the full year.
Its 1996 first-half profit, reported last week, was 175.8 million francs, up 36 percent.
"We're certain the second half results will bolster those of the first," Douay said.
He said last year's troubles were due to a raft of product launches and cost pressures, while launches this year were at a steady level and "purchasing costs are oriented lower".
"The production forecasts we've received from clients don't indicate a slowdown in activity, France included," he said. Bertrand Faure generates 70 percent of its sales outside France.

Dewavrin said the Delsey luggage unit, which Bertrand Faure wants to sell, would show a profit in the second half after a loss of 28 million francs on sales of 368 million francs in the first. "Our idea was to bring it back to profit before selling Delsey," he said. "Delsey will make money next year."
Bertrand Faure also confirmed it still planned to sell its Ratier-Figeac aerospace unit, which contributed a 23 million franc profit in the first half on sales of 293 million.
